title: Epoxide opening in acid
subtitle: Methanol attacks the more substituted carbon of a protonated epoxide

reactants.caption: 2,2-dimethyloxirane + methanol + sulfuric acid
hintTiers: Methanol is a weak nucleophile and the neutral epoxide oxygen is a poor leaving group. What does the acid do to the epoxide oxygen?
The epoxide oxygen takes the acidic proton of sulfuric acid, and the O–H pair stays on the acid's oxygen. Two arrows.
Epoxide oxygen lone pair → new bond to the acidic proton of H₂SO₄; that O–H bond → a lone pair on the sulfuric acid oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Neutral methanol is too weak a nucleophile to open a neutral epoxide. Protonate the epoxide oxygen first.

protonated-epoxide.caption: protonated epoxide + methanol + hydrogensulfate
protonated-epoxide.learnerPrompt: Methanol opens the ring. Which carbon does it attack?
hintTiers: In the protonated epoxide the C–O bonds are weakened, and the bond to the tertiary carbon is the longer and weaker one: that carbon carries most of the positive charge.
Methanol bonds to the tertiary carbon and the C–O bond to that carbon breaks, its pair going to the epoxide oxygen. Two arrows.
Methanol oxygen lone pair → new bond to the carbon carrying the two methyl groups; that C–O bond → a lone pair on the epoxide oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: Under basic conditions this is where the nucleophile goes. Under acid, the C–O bond to the tertiary carbon is the weaker one and that carbon carries more positive charge, so methanol attacks the more substituted carbon.
Hydrogensulfate is a very weak nucleophile, and there is only a little of it. The solvent, methanol, opens the ring.

partialProgressMessages.feedbackMessage: Right bond to break, but a free tertiary cation does not form: the product has the methoxy group on the face opposite the oxygen (inversion). Methanol attacks as the bond breaks: add that arrow.

oxonium-ion.caption: protonated ether + hydrogensulfate
hintTiers: The methanol oxygen now has three bonds and a positive charge. Which base was made in the first step?
Hydrogensulfate takes the proton from the positive oxygen; the O–H pair stays on that oxygen. Two arrows.
Hydrogensulfate oxygen lone pair → new bond to the drawn H on the positive oxygen; that O–H bond → a lone pair on the oxygen.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: That proton belongs to a neutral OH group. Remove the one on the positive oxygen.

steps.explanationAfterStep: The epoxide oxygen is protonated: now it leaves as a neutral alcohol oxygen, and the ring is ready to open.

Methanol attacks the more substituted carbon. The reaction is SN2-like (inversion at that carbon), but with a lot of SN1 character: the C–O bond to the tertiary carbon is well stretched before methanol arrives, so that carbon carries most of the positive charge, and charge decides where the nucleophile goes. The app does not check stereochemistry yet.
Loss of the proton gives the ether and returns sulfuric acid: the acid is a catalyst.

mechanismSummary: The acid protonates the epoxide oxygen. In the protonated epoxide the bond to the tertiary carbon is weakened most and that carbon carries most of the positive charge, so methanol attacks there, from the face opposite the oxygen. Loss of a proton gives 2-methoxy-2-methylpropan-1-ol. Under basic conditions the regiochemistry is the opposite. The app does not check stereochemistry yet.
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 15
